stage_objective: Moves toward first on contact, without watching the ball.
Decides before the bag whether to run through first or round it.
Hits the inside corner of each base and stays low through the turn.
Slides on the seat in a figure-four with both hands up.
Finishes the slide on their feet and reads whether to take the next base.
Takes a primary and a secondary lead timed to the pitch.
Breaks on the pitcher's first move toward home, not on a guess.
Leaves on the catch — not before it, not a beat after.
gap_notes: THIN. One drill serves this stage. Its own three rounds carry the progression, but a coach has no second station to rotate a group through.

stage_name: Reading a ball in the dirt
stage_objective: Advances only when the ball actually gets past the catcher.

stage_name: Running the bases in a game
stage_objective: Makes the right call on every base without a coach telling them.
Sets up balanced, athletic and repeatable without being reminded.
Holds the bat with the knocking knuckles roughly aligned, without adjusting mid-swing.
Moves weight into the back hip and can hold it there, without leaning backwards.

stage_name: Load to launch, and the stride
stage_objective: Front foot lands with the hands still back, in a repeatable place, every swing.
Rotates around a centred axis with the hips leading, rather than sliding forward.
Hands travel to the ball ahead of the barrel, with the elbow in and no loop.
Makes contact out in front of the front foot and drives the ball on a line.
Tracks a moving ball and drives it on a line, with the head still through contact.
Changes posture and path to match the height and side of the pitch.
Changes approach with the count and puts the ball in play on purpose.
Receives the ball moving toward the zone, with the glove quiet after the catch.
Beats the ball to the spot and holds borderline pitches inside the zone.
Drops into a blocking shape that deadens the ball in front of the plate.
gap_notes: THIN. One drill serves this stage. Its own three internal stages carry it, but a coach has no alternative station to rotate to.

stage_objective: Reads and blocks a ball in the dirt without pre-setting to a side.
Transfers during the footwork and delivers an accurate throw to the bag.
Receives from one knee while staying able to block and throw.
Gets low with the chest over the toes and stays there between reps.
Sets the glove before the ball arrives and covers with the throwing hand.

stage_name: Approach and getting around the ball
stage_objective: Arrives at the ball moving forward, having taken an angle rather than a straight line.
Adjusts to a ball that does not bounce true, and receives the short hop with a soft glove.
Meets the ball in front of the front foot, with the glove visible and the eyes on it.
Gets the ball from glove to throwing hand in one motion, in front of the chest.
Steps toward the target after fielding, with the body aligned before the arm works.
Delivers a catchable, chest-high throw to a target after a live ground ball.
Gets to balls either side of the body and still fields them cleanly.
Makes the play under time pressure, including when the first attempt goes wrong.
Executes the plays their actual position is responsible for.
Is moving on contact rather than watching, with the first step taking ground.
Opens the hips and turns to run on a ball hit overhead, rather than backpedalling.

stage_name: Tracking a ball in the air
stage_objective: Keeps eyes on the ball into the glove and arrives set rather than still moving.
Catches a ball coming down without flinching or turning away.
Runs an efficient route to where the ball will be, not to where it is.
Calls the ball early and loudly, and yields audibly when called off.
Fields a ball on the ground in the outfield while moving through it.
gap_notes: The routine ground ball and the knee-down block are now covered by their own row, and do-or-die has moved to the progression slot it belongs in. Still missing: the ball played off a fence. That is deferred rather than forgotten — most fields these teams play on have no fence, so the leverage is low.

stage_objective: Gets the whole body behind a long throw after catching.

stage_name: Throws to bases and the cutoff
stage_objective: Throws through the cutoff man to the right base.
Charges, fields on the move and throws home with the game on the line.
Picks the right base, the right call and the right risk, without being told.
Warms up and recovers the same way every outing, without being told.
Holds the top of the delivery still for two seconds without wobbling.
Can be stopped at any checkpoint of the motion and hold that position.
Moves the front hip toward the plate before the shoulders follow.
Lands the front foot in the same place, pointing the same way, every pitch.
Pulls the glove into the ribs so the chest drives at the target.
Moves the arm loosely and snaps the wrist, producing tight backspin.
Releases the ball at the same point out front on every pitch.
Finishes balanced, decelerated, and ready to field.
Moves down the mound with rhythm rather than from a standstill.
Throws a changeup for a strike with the same arm speed as the fastball.
Finds a four-seam grip without looking and lets the ball go without fear.
Takes the ball down and through with the elbow at shoulder height and a wrist snap.
Lines the body up at the target before the arm works.
Uses the legs and torso so the throw is not made by the arm alone.
Catches cleanly and throws back with full mechanics, repeatedly.
Gets the feet organised on the move so the throw can be made from anywhere.
Releases without a visible pause between the catch and the throw.
Throws at a specific spot and keeps doing so under mild pressure.
Builds arm strength at distance with an arc, and looks after the arm afterwards.
Keeps the mechanics under real urgency, after a real play.
Makes the throws their position is actually asked for.
